notes.text: The auto-reset pair. `.dtr` and `.rts` go to the bridge's DTR and RTS, `.en` to the module's EN and `.boot` to its GPIO0.
SW2, BOOT: pulls GPIO0 to ground.
The USB-UART bridge (U3), on the first receptacle.
R11: pulls the bridge's reset line up to VBUS.
C3: the decoupling of the bridge's own 3.3 V (VDD), which the board does not use as a supply (the author's notes: it gives 100 mA only).
C4 and C8 on EN (the module's 100 nF for power-up timing, and the second), C9 on GPIO0.
R1: EN's 10 kohm pull-up (Espressif's circuit; the module needs EN driven).
The development board's two 22-pin headers (U2), hand-soldered.
The module (U1): 4 MB of flash, PCB antenna.
D1: lit from VBUS through R6.
The 3.3 V regulator (U5), an AMS1117-3.3 in a SOT-223 (a row of the project's catalog).
SW1, RESET: pulls EN to ground.
R10: holds the bridge's SUSPENDb output low.
J2: the receptacle of the module's own USB.
J1: the receptacle of the bridge.
D2 and D3: each receptacle's VBUS reaches VBUS through a Schottky diode (anode on the receptacle), so the two supplies cannot feed each other. ROHM RB161QS-40.
D4: GPIO38 through R9.
The 3.3 V of the regulator: the module's supply and the header's 3.3 V pins.
C5, C7 and C10: the module's 100 nF and 22 uF on 3.3 V, and the regulator's output capacitor (22 uF).
VBUS behind the two diodes: the bridge's supply, the regulator's input and the header's 5 V pin.
C1 and C2: the bridge's VBUS input, 1 uF and 100 nF (CP2102N datasheet, as the author's notes say).
C6: the regulator's input, 22 uF tantalum.
.power_led_resistor.current == (.vbus.voltage - .power_led.forward_voltage) / .power_led_resistor.resistance
